text: Mastermind, launch a minion to look into the Servex code repository that is somewhere in my C drive's code folder. It's just a couple folders up, maybe one folder up, probably two folders up. Anyway, it's like a server manager and I don't remember exactly how the repo is structured. There might be a git submodule for the server itself, which is probably a stale repo, I think I've restructured and now the server is just baked into this monorepo. So do we have a Servex? I think maybe what we want to do is just move the Servex code in here, alongside the server. Look into the Servex thing. What it is, what it does. Whether it would work. The whole API, the CLI, the path, environment variables or whatever, to get it to work properly is definitely a big question. Do we npm install it globally or locally or npx it? I'm not as familiar with designing command line APIs. I'm not sure I really want to lean into a sophisticated API. I think the Servex idea is mostly you just start this thing up and it just runs on its own. I do now recall that it was using PM2, which might be a little bit overkill but might have some useful features. Generally I lean into rewriting things, especially now that we have AI and we're developing these systems. It might be better to just build it ourselves so we can have our own UI, update the UI how we want, configure features, etc.
